title: The Impersonal Style of the Law

sections.content: You know nouns made from actions, such as *la subida de los precios*, from B2 Unit 21, and impersonal *se* from B1 Unit 6. Legal Spanish combines them. Nobody forbids, nobody expels, nobody pays: things are prohibited, expulsion is carried out, non-payment has consequences. The agent disappears and the rule seems to speak by itself. *Queda prohibido el uso de…* replaces "nobody may use". *Se procederá a la expulsión del socio* replaces "the board will expel the member". *El impago de la cuota* replaces "if a member does not pay the fee".

sections.title: Plain version and legal version
rows: Nadie puede usar la parcela de otro socio.
Queda prohibido el uso de la parcela de otro socio.
Se procederá a la expulsión del socio.
Si un socio no paga la cuota, perderá la parcela.
El impago de la cuota será motivo de pérdida de la parcela.
Si un socio incumple el reglamento, la junta lo amonestará.
El incumplimiento del reglamento será motivo de amonestación.

items.spanish: Queda prohibido el uso de las herramientas comunes sin permiso.
items.english: The use of the shared tools without permission is prohibited.

items.spanish: Se procederá a la expulsión del socio que incumpla el reglamento.
items.english: The member who breaches the regulation will be expelled.

items.spanish: El impago de la cuota será motivo de amonestación.
items.english: Non-payment of the fee will be grounds for a warning.

items.spanish: El incumplimiento del reglamento podrá dar lugar a una sanción.
items.english: Breach of the regulation may lead to a penalty.

sections.content: English gets the same effect with passives ("is hereby prohibited"), but a Spanish rule rarely names who acts. With *se procederá a*, the verb stays singular: *se procederá a la expulsión*, never *se procederán*. Use this style for rules and notices, and the plain verb in everyday talk: a friend who hears *queda prohibido* from you will think you are reading a sign.
